title.narrative: Joint Programme on Housing, Land and Property Issues - Phase II

description.narrative: The overall objective of the project is to contribute to the creation of an enabling environment where crisis affected women and men and communities can exercise their HLP rights. The proposed Action is a continuation of Phase I. Acknowledging the spirit of the proposed activities in building upon the rich analytical work produced in Phase I, with a view to applying the results towards effecting meaningful change within the HLP landscape in Phase II, a six-month Inception Period is proposed. It is anticipated that during this period, close liaison with EU counterparts will be required to agree the final details of the programmatic direction of Phase II interventions. As Phase I outcomes have shown, the acute sensitivities which surround HLP interventions in the Syrian context, require a particularly cautious and astute approach to ensure full adherence to do-no-harm principles. It is the preference of the Joint Programme Partners to allow for an adequate space set out within the Phase II timeline to account for a duration of effectual liaising and strategizing to mitigate risks. It is felt by project partners that consensus, shared vision, agreed perspective of risk and strong harmony across the sequencing and scope of Phase II interventions, will be paramount to ensuring absolute diligence to do-no-harm principles and will allow for confidence among partners and donors alike as analysis transitions to interventions. Furthermore, owing to the need to take account of the findings and recommendations from the Communications and Dissemination Strategy (expected to be delivered by December 2021), the partners foresee the need for a period of time in which to clarify or incorporate specific aspects of the programme design in line with the guidance of the Strategy. The proposed activities of Phase II capture a broad spectrum of interventions based upon the achievements of Phase I. While the joint partners will use this period to work out and jointly agree specific approaches to activities, in the interest of maintaining traction and in order to not lose momentum on a number of critical issues introduced in Phase I, a number of activities that are well established will continue or simply roll-over into the new phase (e.g. legal awareness and counselling). It is therefore anticipated that for many activities, progress can move ahead from the onset of Phase II, considering the practice/experience of the responsible agency, level of associated risk, etc. For other activities, which require deeper strategizing to design the intervention, scope and necessary nuancing to context, initiatives may require a piloting approach followed by review and possible course corrections etc. Furthermore, it is foreseen that certain areas of activities including capacity building, communications/ advocacy and risk, are likely to benefit from a system of deeper coordination than what is currently offered at the TWG level. The Inception Phase will allow time and negotiation among partners to agree on the coordination needs and thus workable mechanisms to have in place to facilitate close alliance on these issues. The project will include inception phase which is a transition from Phase I. The Inception duration is also intended to allow for a period of enhanced liaison with the donor to enable a thorough understanding vis-à-vis donor concerns relating to the finer details of programming such as beneficiary targeting, delivery modalities etc. as may be associated with specific activities. This will also address lessons learned from Phase I, where interpretations of donor concerns could be open to subjectivity. An agreed period of time in which to jointly and transparently agree to key foundational aspects of activities, will set a confident trajectory for delivery once the project matures beyond its initial six months. The duration of the Action is 36 months, including a 6-month inception phase to bridge between Phase I and Phase II. A summary workplan is attached as Annex 4. During the inception phase, partners will develop detailed workplans that will be shared with the EU for review and approval after which they will be used for overall coordination.
